analysis:
CHANGELOG.md only: base units 11 and 12 are historical v0.8.x/v0.5.0 entries, and head unit 13 (lines 1-208) adds the v0.10.1 candidate notes. No executable code, controls or configuration changed, so I found no direct security regression. The notes describe behavior changes whose implementations were not supplied. Next passes should check these against the code.

1. Weight-hash reuse (head lines 48-50). The cached verified-weights.json record is trusted while device, inode, size, mtime and ctime match. This touches A-004, T-012 and T-027. Because ADV-001 is the root-capable operator (TB-003), this could weaken weight-substitution detection if the record is not integrity-bound to an attested state. Check that the record is owner-only, that the check is fail-closed, and that clock manipulation or in-place mmap writes cannot reuse a stale hash. The coordinator weight-hash check is already weak under SEC-007, so the delta may be small.

2. Autopilot (head lines 90-98). Downloads happen on the operator's behalf, models adopted after an operation's lease ends keep serving, and weight-hash verification gates holds. Check the coordinator-to-provider trust path, disk exhaustion (T-016), catalog authenticity, and that the 50 GiB free-disk floor is enforced.

3. Desktop control API and LaunchAgent (head lines 100-117). This is a new loopback authenticated local API with a read-only session. It is new local attack surface, with no matching threat-model entry or TB covering it. Check the auth token handling, origin and DNS-rebinding protections, and the stale-service replacement logic.

4. Page-cache availability accounting (head lines 73-77) affects admission and capacity only. Check that it does not cause memory over-admission and denial of service (T-029).

5. Other items: the Nemotron media body bound increase to 40 MiB (head lines 58-62; check DoS bounds), GLM JSON/tool validation (fail-closed, no plaintext leak), and the mlx-swift-lm pin bump, which was not inspected.

The threat model may need updates for the desktop API and Autopilot downloads. No cache-storage (T-041) or attestation behavior change is described.
